newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST-Saga's T197 pre-tax seen at NOK 456 mln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Saga's T197 pre-tax seen at NOK 456 mln.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA is expected to book pre-tax profits in the first tertial of 456 million crowns, according to a Reuter poll of nine Norwegian and foreign analysts.
There was no comparative figure for a year ago as the result for the 1997 period includes earnings from North Sea explorer Santa Fe Exploration, which Saga formally acquired in December.

Analysts' estimates varied widely as expected large losses on foreign exchange transactions, tax-related considerations and the inclusion of Santa Fe for the first time had made projections unclear for the four-month period, they said.
Net financial items, including losses on foreign exchange transactions, varied from minus 1.40 billion crowns to minus 692 million crowns. Most put forex losses at around one billion crowns.
"We should be glad that Saga is priced more from the net asset value than from the income of any specific tertial," said one of the analysts.
Three of the analysts recommended to buy the stock, three said hold, two said sell and one declined to give a recommendation.
"It's no secret that there will be a large currency loss, but the problem is that not even Saga itself seems sure how exactely this will be treated in the financial statement," another analyst said.
Analysts also said investors were sceptical to put any new value in the share based on additional gas discoveries. Investor-confidence was based more in oil finds, they said.
